title: Angular Averaging Identity from Sphere Measure Theory
description: Proves the 2D angular averaging identity ∫_0^π |cos θ| dθ = 2 from first principles, constructing an axiom-free AngularAverageData 2 instance. Derives the product formula c_n · c_{n+1} = 2/(n·π) for Cauchy-Crofton constants using the sphere area recurrence. The 2D case confirms that E[crossings] = 2L/(πd) requires no measure-theoretic axioms.

openQuestion.question: Can the angular averaging identity ∫_{S^{n-1}} |⟨v, ω⟩| dσ(ω) = 2σ_{n-2}/(n-1) · ‖v‖ be proved from Mathlib's sphere measure theory?
openQuestion.answer: Yes for n=2: proved via ∫_0^π |cos θ| dθ = 2 (rotation of the known ∫_0^π |sin θ| dθ = 2). For n ≥ 3: requires the Beta integral ∫_0^{π/2} cos(θ) sin^{n-2}(θ) dθ = 1/(n-1), which is axiomatized.

highlights: 2D angular averaging proved axiom-free: AngularAverageData 2 from interval integration
Product formula c_n · c_{n+1} = 2/(n·π) derived from sphere area recurrence
The 2D Cauchy-Crofton constant c_2 = 2/π verified from first principles
General n-dim case axiomatized with clear Beta integral proof path

implications.statement: E[crossings] = 2L/(πd) requires no axioms for n=2
c_n · c_{n+1} is strictly decreasing: the constants tend to 0

assumptions: angularAvg_ndim: for n ≥ 3, the sphere integral ∫_{S^{n-1}} |ω₁| dσ = 2σ_{n-2}/(n-1) (requires Beta integral via polar coordinates on S^{n-1})
